BiblicalUsage: Gomorrah was one of the cities of the plain, and its name is almost never spoken without Sodom's beside it: the LORD rained brimstone and fire on both cities out of heaven, Moses warned Israel that their land could end up looking like Sodom and Gomorrah if they turned away, and Isaiah told Judah that only a small remnant kept them from sharing the same fate. After Genesis 19 the city is a byword for judgment, not a place anyone goes back to.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Gomorrah stands in Scripture as the warning that judgment is real and sudden, and that mercy is the only reason any of us are not left like it. Isaiah's remnant is the hope in the story: God always keeps a people, even when the cities around them fall.
